interest: Shows wartime Axis propaganda on Japan's cotton expansion in Southeast Asia, debunked by Japanese sources citing shipping shortages.
overview: File (1941-43): a 1941 cotton-trade note from Anderson, Clayton & Co.; German propaganda claims Japan would expand Philippine and Celebes cotton to supply Europe, which British intelligence quoting Japanese sources dismisses, citing slow progress and a massive shipping backlog.

people.name: Lamar Fleming, Jr.
people.role: Representative / partner of Anderson, Clayton & Co.

people.name: Maxwell M. Hamilton
people.role: Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, U.S. Department of State

people.name: H. Freeman Matthews
people.role: U.S. Chargé d'Affaires ad interim in London

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a letter from Anderson, Clayton & Co. discussing its cotton trade with Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Anderson, Clayton & Co. reports on its ongoing cotton trade with Japan, offering to discuss further.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Anderson, Clayton & Co. Cotton Trade with Japan

subfiles.about: Reports German economic propaganda alleging Japanese plans to cultivate cotton in Southeast Asia for export to Europe and Asia.
subfiles.summary: Harrison reports German propaganda claiming Japan will convert Philippine and Celebes sugar land to cotton for Europe, which he identifies as a bid to downplay reliance on American imports.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Harrison (Bern) on German Economic Propaganda Regarding Japanese Cotton Expansion

subfiles.about: Transmits British intelligence reporting Japanese admissions of lagging cotton cultivation and severe shipping bottlenecks.
subfiles.summary: British intelligence, citing Japan's own press, says occupied-area cotton expansion has barely started amid a massive shipping backlog.
subfiles.title: Airgram from Matthews (London) Transmitting British Intelligence on Japanese Cotton and Shipping Shortages
